legacy_quote: Re-verification of hygiene performance shall be carried out not later than ninety days after the previous verification is signed off.
target_article_text:
Article 118 - Hygiene Verification for Wet Processing Lines
(1) Wet processing lines shall be drained and inspected at each scheduled shutdown before
cleaning agents are introduced.
(2) Verification records shall identify the line segment, the cleaning agent batch, and the
responsible operator.
(3) Re-verification of hygiene performance shall be carried out not later than ninety days after the
previous verification is signed off.

legacy_quote: Every chemical transfer hose shall carry a durable label showing the transferred substance and the last pressure test date.
target_article_text:
Article 133 - Labeling of Chemical Transfer Hoses
(1) Every chemical transfer hose shall carry a durable label showing the transferred substance and
the last pressure test date.

legacy_quote: Interlock function shall be proof tested at intervals not exceeding twelve months and the proof test shall be recorded.
target_article_text:
Article 147 - Guarding of Rotating Equipment
(1) Rotating shafts, couplings, and belt drives shall be enclosed by fixed guards that cannot be
removed without a tool.
(2) Where access is required during operation, interlocks shall bring the equipment to a safe state
before the guard is opened.
(3) Interlock function shall be proof tested at intervals not exceeding twelve months and the proof
test shall be recorded.

legacy_quote: A competent person shall attempt a start under the lockout and confirm zero energy state before work proceeds.
target_article_text:
Article 156 - Lockout Verification Before Maintenance
(1) Energy isolation devices shall be locked in the de-energized position before any maintenance
work begins.
(2) A competent person shall attempt a start under the lockout and confirm zero energy state
before work proceeds.

legacy_quote: The set pressure of every relief device shall not exceed the vessel design pressure and shall be stamped on the device nameplate.
target_article_text:
Article 163 - Pressure Relief on Steam Vessels
(1) Each steam vessel shall be fitted with at least one pressure relief device sized for the maximum
steam input.
(2) The set pressure of every relief device shall not exceed the vessel design pressure and shall be
stamped on the device nameplate.
(3) Relief discharge shall be routed to a safe location away from occupied areas and shall be
inspected for obstruction monthly.

legacy_quote: Weekly activation checks shall confirm flow, temperature, and unobstructed access, and the checks shall be logged.
target_article_text:
Article 177 - Emergency Showers in Corrosive Areas
(1) An emergency shower and eyewash station shall be provided within fifteen metres of any
corrosive chemical transfer point.
(2) Weekly activation checks shall confirm flow, temperature, and unobstructed access, and the
checks shall be logged.

legacy_quote: The air change rate in each storage room shall be maintained at not less than twelve air changes per hour during transfer operations.
target_article_text:
Article 193 - Ventilation in Solvent Storage Rooms
(1) Solvent storage rooms shall be ventilated continuously during occupied hours and shall be
posted with a no ignition notice.
(2) Ventilation fans shall be interlocked with the room lighting circuit so that lighting cannot be
energized while fans are stopped.
(3) The air change rate in each storage room shall be maintained at not less than twelve air
changes per hour during transfer operations.

legacy_quote: Calibration logs for safety critical instruments shall be retained for not less than seven years after the last entry.
target_article_text:
Article 205 - Record Retention for Calibration Logs
(1) Calibration logs for safety critical instruments shall be retained for not less than seven years
after the last entry.

legacy_quote: A transport manifest listing every cylinder by gas and quantity shall accompany each load.
target_article_text:
Article 213 - Transport of Compressed Gas Cylinders
(1) Compressed gas cylinders shall be transported in an upright position with valve protection caps
fitted.
(2) Cylinders shall be secured against movement by chocks, wedges, or a purpose built cradle
during transport.
(3) Cylinders of flammable gases shall be separated from oxidizing gases by at least three metres
during transport.
(4) A transport manifest listing every cylinder by gas and quantity shall accompany each load.
